top.logout.title: Unpair this device
top.logout.confirm: Unpair this device? You will need to scan the QR code again.
chart.temp.title: Temperatures · last 10 min
chart.temp.aria: CPU and GPU temperature over the last 10 minutes
chart.rpm.title: Fans · RPM · last 10 min
chart.rpm.aria: Motherboard fan RPM over the last 10 minutes
chart.rpm.noFans: This motherboard reports no fans to FanPilot.
chart.rpm.none: No fan is reporting RPM right now.
chart.rpm.silent: No RPM reading (0): {fans}. They are left out of the chart.
fans.title: Motherboard fans
fans.sub: tap a fan to adjust it
fans.softwareCurves: On this board FanPilot runs the curves: when it closes, the fans go back to BIOS control.
fans.unsupported: This motherboard ({board}) has no fan control through the path FanPilot uses.
turbo.banner: Turbo is on: every motherboard fan at 100% (the GPU is not affected). Tap again to go back to the previous settings.
profiles.afterTurbo: Takes effect when Turbo goes off
response.fast.desc: follows the temperature almost at once and slows down after cooling 1 °C.
response.balanced.desc: ignores spikes of a few seconds and only slows down after cooling 2 °C.
response.smooth.desc: ignores spikes of about 10 s, changes speed slowly and only slows down after cooling 4 °C.
orphan.text: The settings saved for "{name}" match no fan on this board and were not applied.
ed.turboOn: Turn Turbo off to adjust a single fan.
ed.profileNote: The {profile} profile is on: applying or restoring here turns it off, and the other fans keep its curve as their own setting.
ed.fixedHint.chip: Protection: the chip still goes to 100% if the sensor goes above {temp} °C.
ed.fixedHint.app: Protection: FanPilot still goes to 100% if the sensor goes above {temp} °C.
ed.limits: At least {min}% at any point; 100% at {max} °C at the latest.
ed.limits.chip: The curve runs in the motherboard's chip (it keeps working even if the PC or FanPilot closes).
ed.limits.app: FanPilot runs the curve every second. If it closes, or the reference sensor stops answering, the fan goes back to BIOS control.
ed.limits.socket: The curve follows the board's sensor (its "CPU" is the socket one); the CPU card shows the cores' temperature.
ed.response.hint: {name}: {desc} With any response, at the curve's last point the fan goes to 100% at once.
ed.applied.app: Applied: FanPilot is controlling this fan
ed.restored.bios: Fan handed back to BIOS control
ed.discard.question: Discard changes?
ed.discard.text: What you changed here hasn't been applied yet.
ed.points.aria: Curve points: drag them, or use the arrow keys
ed.tune.hint: Tap a point to adjust it one step at a time. With a keyboard: Tab to the point and use the arrow keys (with Shift, 5 at a time).
ed.tune.label: Point {i} of {n}: {t} °C, {p}%
ed.pumpNote: Protected pump: anything applied here becomes 100%. To allow another speed, change the protection under "Name and role".
ed.meta.name: Name
ed.meta.hint: The name shows on the panel and the charts, with the original next to it. On a pump, nothing FanPilot applies goes below the protection: not the editor, not Turbo, not a profile.
gpu.safety: {n}% · back to automatic at {temp} °C or more
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.settings: Limits and notifications outside the panel
alerts.privacy: Nothing leaves the PC without a destination here, and the messages carry only the alert and the PC's name. The ntfy address and the token are kept encrypted on this PC; a field left blank keeps what is already saved. The messages go out in this panel's language.
pair.title: Pair a phone
pair.scan: Scan it with the phone's camera (on the same Wi-Fi network). The code works once and changes every few minutes.
pair.firewall: If the phone can't connect: allow the port in the firewall (scripts\firewall.ps1) and check that the Windows network is set to "Private".
locked.title: 🔒 Device not paired
locked.how: On the PC, open {url} (it opens by itself when FanPilot starts) and scan the QR code with this device's camera.
locked.hint: The QR code lasts a few minutes and works only once.
err.tooManyStreams: Too many panel connections at once: close a tab or a device.
err.noFanControl: This motherboard offers no fan control through FanPilot.
err.globalMode: Invalid mode: use custom or profile:quiet, profile:standard, profile:performance.
err.turboOn: Turn Turbo off to adjust a single fan.
err.turboPump: Turn Turbo off to change the pump's role or protection.
err.response: Invalid response: use fast, balanced or smooth.
err.curve.points: This fan's curve needs exactly {n} points.
err.curve.increasing: The curve's temperatures must go up.
err.curve.maxTemp: Highest temperature allowed in the curve: {max} °C.
err.curve.shape: The curve needs at least 3 points, the last one at 255.
err.noBios: This board doesn't hand fans back to the BIOS.
err.orphan.exists: That fan exists on this board: use "Restore original" on it.
err.meta.labelLength: The name can have up to {n} characters.
err.meta.labelControl: The name can't have line breaks or tabs.
err.meta.role: Invalid role: use fan or pump.
err.meta.pumpPolicy: Invalid pump protection: use full or min.
err.meta.pumpMin: The pump's minimum goes from {min}% to 100%.
err.alerts.cpu: The CPU limit goes from {min} to {max} °C.
err.alerts.gpu: The GPU limit goes from {min} to {max} °C.
err.alerts.pcName: The PC name goes from 1 to {max} characters.
err.alerts.ntfy: The ntfy address is the topic's, for example https://ntfy.sh/fanpilot-abc123.
err.alerts.telegram: Telegram needs the bot token and the chat id.
err.alerts.noDestination: Set up ntfy or Telegram before the test.
server.starting: FanPilot is starting. Try again in a few seconds.
server.pairLocalOnly: Pairing can only be opened on the PC itself.
server.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute.
server.codeInvalid: Invalid or expired code. Scan the QR code again.
notice.gccFallback: Gigabyte Control Center {version} is not compatible with this FanPilot ({problem}): using LibreHardwareMonitor instead.
notice.alertsOtherPc: The alert destinations (alerts.json) were saved on another PC and can't be read here: set them up again.
notice.configInvalid: config.json is invalid; using the defaults until it is fixed: {detail}
notice.fileUnreadable.previous: {file} was unreadable ({problem}) and was set aside as {aside}; using the previous version.
notice.fileUnreadable.fresh: {file} was unreadable ({problem}) and was set aside as {aside}; FanPilot started without it.
notice.backupLost.one: No original curve for {fans}: the backup was lost while FanPilot controlled that fan. "Restore original" is unavailable for it.
notice.backupLost.other: No original curve for {fans}: the backup was lost while FanPilot controlled those fans. "Restore original" is unavailable for them.
gcc.incompatible: Gigabyte Control Center {version} is not compatible with this FanPilot ({problem}).
startup.gccMissing: config.json asks for "backend": "gigabyte", but Gigabyte Control Center was not found (looked in {dir}).
board.tempInputRefused: The service refused to change the temperature sensor.
board.noGen3: This motherboard doesn't expose the GCC's third-generation fan control.
board.pawnioMissing: The PawnIO driver is missing, and without it the motherboard's sensors can't be read nor its fans controlled. Close and reopen FanPilot to install it (or download it from https://pawnio.eu).
board.noSuperIo: LibreHardwareMonitor did not recognize this motherboard's sensor chip. This is common on laptops: the maker controls the fans through its own firmware.
board.noSuperIo.named: LibreHardwareMonitor did not recognize the sensor chip of this motherboard ({board}). This is common on laptops: the maker controls the fans through its own firmware.
board.noControl: The {chips} chip was recognized, but LibreHardwareMonitor can't control its fans.
board.problem.sensor: {fan}: no valid reading from the reference sensor; on the BIOS until it comes back.
board.problem.lhm: LibreHardwareMonitor stopped answering: every fan is on the BIOS until it comes back.
gpu.noNvml: NVML not found (nvml.dll): install the NVIDIA driver.
gpu.noFans: The GPU exposes no fans that can be controlled.
gpu.refusedNvml: The driver refused manual fan control (NVML {code}).
gpu.refused: The driver refused manual fan control: {detail}
gpu.lhmNoControl: LibreHardwareMonitor can't control this GPU's fan.
gpu.safetyNote: Fan back on automatic: the GPU reached {temp} °C ({time})
cpu.hint.pawnio: Install PawnIO (pawnio.eu) to see the cores' temperature.
alert.boardDown.title: Board sensors unavailable
alert.boardDown.detail: The motherboard hasn't answered for more than a minute. Check the maker's service and FanPilot's log.
alert.control.title: Control handed back to the BIOS
alert.fanStopped.title: Fan stopped: {name}
alert.pumpStopped.title: Pump stopped: {name}
alert.stopped.detail: Reads {rpm} RPM at {duty}% commanded; it was spinning before.
alert.temp.title: {what} at {temp} °C
alert.temp.detail: Above the {limit} °C limit for more than 10 s.
alert.resolved.title: Resolved: {title}
alert.test.title: Alert test
alert.test.detail: If you are reading this, FanPilot's alerts arrive here.
console.unknownScenario: Unknown fake board scenario: {scenario}. Use one of: {list}.
console.admin: FanPilot needs to run as Administrator (reaching the motherboard's sensors and fans requires it).
console.hwtestBusy: Close FanPilot before the hardware test: the two would fight over the fans.
console.import.busy: Stop FanPilot (or the service) before importing: it is using the data right now.
console.import.same: The source folder is the data folder itself.
console.portBusy: Could not open port {port} ({detail}). Another program is probably using it: close it or change "port" in config.json.
console.noAdmin: Without Administrator: the panel only opens at {url} (no phone can pair).
console.running: FanPilot running on port {port}. Network addresses: {urls}
console.pairHint: To pair a phone, open {url} on this PC and scan the QR code.
console.pawnio.notInstalled: PawnIO driver not installed: open FanPilot from its window (without --no-browser) to install it, or download it from {site}.
console.pawnio.why: The PawnIO driver is not installed. Without it FanPilot can't read the motherboard's sensors nor control its fans (it is the driver LibreHardwareMonitor and FanControl use too).
console.pawnio.ask: Install it now with winget (package {id}, from the official site {site})? [Y/n]
console.pawnio.noWinget: winget was not found on this Windows. Download PawnIO from {site}, install it and open FanPilot again.
console.pawnio.installedReboot: PawnIO installed. The installer asked for a restart; if the fans don't show up, restart the PC.
console.pawnio.unfinished: The PawnIO installation did not finish (code {code}). Restart the PC or install it by hand from {site}.
console.pawnio.unfinishedAlready: The PawnIO installation did not finish (code {code}; winget says it is already installed). Restart the PC or install it by hand from {site}.
console.machine.unreadable: machine.json is unreadable; the old curves and pairings were moved to {archive} and won't be applied.
console.machine.other: data\ came from another PC or another motherboard ({board}); the old curves and pairings were moved to {archive} and won't be applied.
diag.howToReport: To report how FanPilot did on this board, open the prefilled form and attach this file: {url}
diag.redacted: Serial numbers and UUIDs were left out.
diag.otherInstance: Note: another FanPilot is running right now; the readings below may reflect its control.
diag.nothingChanged: No fan speed was changed. To report, open the prefilled form and attach that file:
hwtest.interrupting: Stopping: putting the fans and the GPU back as they were…
hwtest.start: Hardware test: about 2 minutes. Ctrl+C stops it and puts everything back as it was.
hwtest.step.curve: Curve for 60 s without the watchdog applying it again
hwtest.step.putBack: Put everything back as it was
hwtest.refuse.noFans: This board offers no fan control through FanPilot: there is nothing to test.
hwtest.refuse.noSuchFan: No such fan. Pick one from 0 to {max} with --fan.
hwtest.refuse.cpuOrPump: '{title}' looks like the CPU fan or a pump: the test leaves it alone. Pick a case fan with --fan.
hwtest.refuse.turbo: Turn Turbo off before the test.
hwtest.refuse.profile: Go back to Custom before the test: a profile is on.
hwtest.refuse.noBackup: '{title}' has no saved original curve: the test couldn't put it back. Pick another fan.
hwtest.abort.ctrlC: Ctrl+C: test stopped by the user.
hwtest.fixed.noTach: no tachometer: only the written curve was checked
hwtest.fail.notWritten: the board didn't keep what was written ({detail})
hwtest.fail.watchdog: the watchdog had to apply the curve again {n} time(s): something (GCC, the BIOS) is overwriting the fans
hwtest.curve.ok: a 40% to 100% curve on for 60 s; the watchdog didn't have to apply it again
hwtest.fail.turboNotBack: {fan} didn't go back to what it was after Turbo
hwtest.turbo.ok: RPM before → with Turbo: {rpms}; when Turbo went off, every fan went back to what it was
hwtest.gpu.noControl: skipped: this GPU's fan can't be controlled
hwtest.fail.gpuNotFixed: the GPU fan didn't stay in fixed mode
hwtest.fail.gpuSpeed: the GPU fan reads {speeds}% instead of 50%
hwtest.fail.gpuNotAuto: the GPU fan didn't go back to automatic
hwtest.fail.notInChip: the curve didn't stay in the chip after closing
hwtest.fail.notBios: the fan didn't go back to the BIOS on closing
hwtest.reopen.chip: the curve stayed in the chip after closing
hwtest.reopen.bios: on closing, the fan went back to the BIOS
hwtest.putBack.user: the user's own setting applied again
hwtest.report.title: # FanPilot · hardware test
